text: The bug is in `TTLCache.expire()`: the while loop condition uses `time > curr.expires` instead of `time >= curr.expires`, while `__contains__`, `__getitem__`, `__delitem__`, and `__iter__` all treat an item as expired when `not (timer() < expires)`, i.e., `timer() >= expires`. This inconsistency means at `t == expires`, other views consider the item expired but `expire()` does not remove it (since `time > curr.expires` is False when equal), so it stays until `t > expires`. The fix is to change `expire()`'s loop condition from `time > curr.expires` to `time >= curr.expires` to be consistent with the rest of the class.
